title: Manitoba calls inquests into 2022 RCMP shooting of Shamattawa man, 2 deaths of people in custody
subtitle: Inquests called into 2022 deaths of inmates at Stony Mountain, Pas Correctional Centre
article: The death of a man shot by RCMP officers in a northern Manitoba First Nation in 2022 will be the focus of one of three inquiries called by the province this week.
Lester Miles, 22, suffered multiple gunshot wounds during an altercation with RCMP on July 2, 2022, a provincial news releases announcing the inquests on Wednesday said.
Both RCMP and the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba, the province's police watchdog, had previously reported the shooting but had not identified Miles by name.

After he was shot, Miles was medevaced to the Health Sciences Centre in Winnipeg, about 750 kilometres to the southwest, where he was declared neurologically dead a few days later. An autopsy found the gunshot wounds caused his death.

The Independent Investigation Unit - which investigates all serious incidents involving police in the province - ultimately cleared the two officers who shot Miles of any wrongdoing, according to its final report , released in January.

Shortly after the shooting, RCMP told Manitoba's police watchdog the officers went to Shamattawa after reports of an intoxicated man walking around the community with a shotgun. Police were told he had shot at the ceiling inside of a home, according to the investigative unit's report.
The two officers who shot Miles declined interviews during the unit's investigation, but provided written statements with their accounts, according to the watchdog's final report.
Both officers said they were searching for Miles in a wooded area of Shamattawa when they heard a shotgun blast nearby and moved toward the sound.
One officer wrote that they found Miles crouching, with a shotgun held perpendicular to his chest. The officers ordered him to drop it before Miles "jerked his hand back," according to the report.
The officer said he shot Miles because he believed the 22-year-old wanted to shoot and kill him and his partner, the IIU report said.
A visual recreation of the scene was included in the report, appearing to show that Miles was shot at least eight times, while several more shots struck nearby.
Two reports from experts in firearms trajectory and the use of force both said the officers' accounts matched the physical and forensic evidence available.
However, the use of force expert noted that "a holistic review of police policies, training and community relations may be warranted to prevent similar incidents in the future," the report says.
An autopsy found Miles had normal blood concentrations of methanol, ethanol, isopropanol and acetone, according to the report.
The watchdog's final report concluded that the officers' use of lethal force against Miles was justified and did not warrant any charges.
The province called inquests into two other deaths from 2022 on Wednesday, both involving men who died after they were found with severe head injuries at correctional facilities.
Nathan Otke, 36, died after he was found unresponsive in his cell at Manitoba's Stony Mountain Institution following an assault, the release said.
He was found to have suffered a skull fracture and traumatic brain injury and died on Feb. 7, 2022, at Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre.
His immediate cause of death was determined to be a traumatic brain injury caused by blunt head trauma.
His death was also ruled a homicide.
The other inquest was called into the death of Tyson Dumas, 34, who was an inmate at The Pas Correctional Centre when he was found unconscious with a head injury on May 25, 2022.
He had been involved in two altercations with other inmates before he was found, according to the province's release.
Dumas suffered a severe brain injury and died at the Health Sciences Centre in Winnipeg on June 4, 2022.
His death was deemed a homicide, with an autopsy showing that he died from a traumatic brain injury caused by blunt force trauma.
The province says information about the date and location of the inquests will be determined by Manitoba's provincial court and released at a later date.
Inquests are conducted to learn more about the circumstances around a death so similar deaths can be prevented in the future.

Under Manitoba's Fatality Inquiries Act, an inquest is required when a person dies as the result of the use of force by an on-duty peace officer. They are also normally required when the person who died was in a custodial facility, unless their death is determined to be the result of natural causes.
